messages:
Maya R: Putting a short thread here — we need to finalize the boundary for policy evaluation at the edge vs control-plane. Two practical constraints: (1) latency-sensitive routes want zero extra RPC hops, (2) ops wants a single fast blast-radius rollback. Thoughts?
Tom S: TL;DR: hybrid execution. Keep scoring primitives local-friendly and push enriched tenant-state to central. But also need deterministic tie-breakers so local and central don't oscillate.
Ivy K: Agree hybrid. A few concrete proposals: (a) define a capability bitmask per router (which signals it can access locally), (b) policy authors must declare signal requirements and an "execution_hint" (local|central|hybrid), and (c) the compiler verifies no misuse (e.g., local policy referencing central-only signal).
Chris D: On the capability bitmask: make it versioned and compact. Something like `cap_v1=0x1 region, 0x2 tenant_tier, 0x4 cost_window`. Routers advertise their bitmask during handshake so control-plane knows what decisions can be offloaded.
Maya R: Important: runtime safety. If local policy sees a signal it believes should be present but it's stale/missing, do NOT apply risky changes — return `SAFE_ROUTE` or the previous route. Log a `policy_mismatch` event.
Tom S: We should add a divergence score emitted every minute per router: fraction_active_requests_where(local_choice != central_choice). Use that to gate local promotion.
Ivy K: For rollout: suggested flow -> author writes policy with `execution_hint: hybrid` -> central deploy + test in central-only canary -> enable local shadowing for 48h (local computes but doesn't act) -> measure divergence and cost-delta -> if below thresholds, promote to active local eval behind a rollout % gate.
Chris D: Also add a simulation step in the CI: run new policy against stored request trace and ensure local/central behavior agrees within tolerance. Fail the CI if variance exceeds X. This prevents teams from marking everyone local by accident.
Maya R: Wire format sketches: central response = `{route_id, score, penalty_ms, confidence, ttl_s, signature}`. Local decision must produce identical schema plus `source:local` in telemetry.
Tom S: Signature is critical. Policy blobs and central verdicts must be signed (KMS) so routers don't apply tampered stakes. Local client validates signature and policy checksum before applying.
Ivy K: Delta distribution: prefer control-plane push over websocket with sequence numbers and ack windows. For flaky routers allow a pull endpoint with compressed gzipped blobs. Keep retention policy short to limit stale policy drift.
Chris D: Edge-case: what if central is slow/backlogged? Local eval should have a policy: if central heartbeat > 500ms, local switches to autonomous mode but uses only conservative rules (e.g., prefer lower-risk routes). Put this threshold in config so ops can tune during incidents.
Maya R: Telemetry fields we need: `policy_id`, `policy_version`, `decision_source`, `matched_rule`, `decision_latency_ms`, `divergence_flag`, `estimated_cost_delta`, `fallback_reason` (if any), `capability_mask`. Keep field names stable.
Tom S: Lint rules: (1) `execution_hint=local` cannot reference `signal:tenant_budget_real_time`, (2) `execution_hint=local` must list only signals present in capability bitmask, (3) `ttl` must be present for central-supplied transient route hints. We'll publish these as part of policy-sdk.
Ivy K: Library plan: publish a spec (protobuf + HTTP endpoints) and reference SDKs in Go + Rust + Python. The router teams can choose embedded library or run a sidecar shim. Sidecar gives looser language support but adds ~0.5ms median. Document tradeoffs.
Chris D: Ops playbook: provide an authenticated /v1/force-fallback endpoint that flips all routers to `SAFE_ROUTE` while the policy team hotfixes. Make it auditable.
ops-bot: Note: added dashboard widgets: `policy_divergence_rate`, `local_fallback_rate`, `avg_local_eval_ms`, `policy_blob_apply_failures`. Alerts set for divergence > 0.5% over 5m.
Maya R: I'll draft an RFC with: execution_hint DSL, capability bitmask spec, telemetry schema, rollout checklist (ci-sim -> central-canary -> local-shadow -> staged-active), delta-push proto sketch, and ops endpoints. Will ping for reviews tomorrow.
Ivy K: Please add migration notes for older policies (automatically mark unspecified as `execution_hint: central` and run CI-sim before auto-promote).
Tom S: +1. Also include a compact example policy snippet for teams to copy: 

policy:
  id: multi_tenant_pref_v1
  execution_hint: hybrid
  signals: [region, tenant_tier, cost_window, budget_flags]
  fallback: SAFE_ROUTE
  metadata: {capability_required: [region,tenant_tier], risk_profile: low}

Maya R: Great. If no objections, I'll draft and include a short proto diff for the delta-push websocket. Thanks all.
